newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down on dollar outflow.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down on dollar outflow.

text.p: Last-minute dollar buying by foreign funds weakened the Philippine peso to 26.374 at the close on Friday from the previous 26.37, traders said.
These funds are those divesting from the local equities market, they said.
The Central Bank had to sell dollars again in late trade to support the local currency after buying dollars in midsession, traders said.
Traders said the last-minute intervention made the Central Bank a net seller of dollars today.
Traders estimate the Central Bank sold some $79 to $73 million at 26.375, and bought about $60 to $59 million at 26.362/26.363.
Before its late intervention, the Central Bank said it was a net buyer of dollars today.

"There is still pressure to get dollars out," one dealer said. But traders said the peso will likely not stray lower than 26.375 because the Central Bank had been determined to keep the peso at that rate.
The Central Bank may again raise its overnight borrowing rate to quell peso speculation, traders said. Late Wednesday, it raised its rate by 0.75 percentage-point to 11 percent as a pre-emptive move.
"The important thing is for the Central Bank to stay at 26.375 and keep interest rates firm," another dealer said.
The day's average was at 26.374 from 26.373. Volume was lower at $315.80 million from $324 million.
